title: Does treating weeds as you drive still beat scouting first when the robot uses published laser-weeder numbers?
lede: re-running the `osrobot-field` weeding model with sourced laser-weeder constants (2 m swath, 0.73 s per weed, 99.2% kill) halves the time but keeps the ranking: inline treatment takes 71.7 min against 79.3 for scout-then-treat at 0.3 weeds/m² and 1 km/h, and scout never wins across densities, speeds and detector hit rates
summary: osrobot-field ran on round numbers. This follow-up replaces the swath (2 m), time per weed (0.73 s) and kill rate (99.2%) with figures from laser-weeding literature and trade sources (read from search summaries, to be re-checked), and sweeps what has no source. Treating inline still beats scout-then-treat with equal kill: at 0.3 weeds/m² and 1 km/h, 71.7 min against 79.3 and 180 Wh against 216; at 3 weeds/m² 110.8 against 133.4 min. Scout never wins in any row. The sourced constants cut the time from 151 to 72 min for the same field. Speed trades kill for area rate (0.65 to 0.38 kill and 0.08 to 0.53 ha/h from 0.5 to 4 km/h); detector hit rate sets kill almost one for one. Stylised and preliminary: the detector hit rate (0.7) and blur law, false positives, mud, energy per metre and beam-steering speed are assumed, kill is limited to a single pass, the laser stops for each weed, and no weed-density source was found (swept 0.3 to 10 per m²).
